claims.text: What the strip looks like Normal sinus rhythm in every way except the rate, which is over 100 bpm.
At very fast rates the P wave can hide in the preceding T wave, giving a “camel hump” look.
claims.quote: With very fast heart rates the P waves may be hidden in the preceding T wave, producing a ‘camel hump’ appearance.

claims.text: P waves: normal sinus P waves, one before every QRS, as in NSR
PR interval: normal and constant, as in NSR
ST segment and T waves: normal, as in NSR
Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Usually secondary to something else — find the cause
claims.quote: Sinus tachycardia is usually a secondary condition.

claims.text: Physiologic and disease: exercise, pain, anxiety, hypovolemia, hypoxia or hypercarbia, acidemia, sepsis or fever, anemia, pulmonary embolism, cardiac tamponade, hyperthyroidism, alcohol withdrawal
claims.quote: Exercise Pain Anxiety Hypovolaemia Hypoxia, hypercarbia Acidaemia Sepsis, pyrexia Anaemia Pulmonary embolism Cardiac tamponade Hyperthyroidism Alcohol withdrawal

claims.text: Drugs: beta-agonists (epinephrine, isoproterenol, albuterol, dobutamine), sympathomimetics (amphetamines, cocaine, methylphenidate), antimuscarinics (antihistamines, TCAs, carbamazepine, atropine), caffeine, theophylline, marijuana
claims.quote: Beta-agonists: adrenaline, isoprenaline, salbutamol, dobutamine Sympathomimetics: amphetamines, cocaine, methylphenidate Antimuscarinics: antihistamines, TCAs, carbamazepine, atropine Others: caffeine, theophylline, marijuana

claims.text: Symptoms May be asymptomatic or cause palpitations (a sense of rapid or forceful beats)
claims.quote: Arrhythmia and conduction disturbances may be asymptomatic or cause palpitations (sensation of skipped beats or rapid or forceful beats)

claims.text: Treatment Treatment is directed at the cause
